title: Latest order per Gold customer, where ties are real
prompt: Nightly retention-email job, always called with @Tier = 'G' (about 150k customers and 3.2M of their orders). It
runs about 9 minutes. The plan scans Orders twice with hash joins and a hash aggregate that spills to tempdb.
Store and Partner imports stamp one timestamp on a whole batch, so about 4% of Gold customers have two or more
orders that share their latest OrderDate. The email lists every latest order. Gold customers with no orders must
data_notes: Azure SQL Database, General Purpose Gen5, 8 vCores, compatibility level 160. READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT ON. Query Store READ_WRITE. Collation SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS. All foreign keys are trusted. Statistics: auto create and auto update ON; a nightly job updates Orders, OrderLines and Payments with FULLSCAN.

Customers: 2.0M rows. Tier S = 1.85M, G = ~150k, P = 25 partner accounts (CustomerID 1 to 25). IsActive = 1 for 88%. Email is NULL for ~9% (~180k rows, ~160k of them active). About 2% of non-NULL emails are shared by two or more customer rows (households). ReferredByCustomerID is non-NULL for 18%; 312 rows are self-referrals (ReferredByCustomerID = CustomerID, CustomerID 500001 to 500312). AccountNumber always matches 'AC' + 10 digits (CHECK constraint).

Orders: 30M rows, 2016 to now, ~12k per day now. The 25 partner customers own ~9M orders (30%), up to 1.2M each. Other customers average ~10 orders (max ~400). The density estimate for CustomerID is ~15 rows. Status: Shipped 83.8%, Cancelled 7%, Paid 6%, Returned 3%, Pending 0.2% (~60k rows, all from the last 72 hours). SalesChannel: Web 62%, Store 20%, Partner 12%, Phone 6%. PromoCode is NULL for 85%. ShipRegionID is NULL for Store pickups (~20%). OrderDate is datetime2(7); Partner and Store imports stamp one timestamp on a whole batch, so many orders of one customer share an OrderDate.
baseline_sql: SELECT c.CustomerID, c.AccountNumber, o.OrderID, o.OrderDate, o.TotalAmount
JOIN qe.Orders o ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID

correct_families.description: One ordered seek per customer that returns every order tied on the latest OrderDate.
reference_sql: SELECT c.CustomerID, c.AccountNumber, lo.OrderID, lo.OrderDate, lo.TotalAmount
SELECT TOP (1) WITH TIES o.OrderID, o.OrderDate, o.TotalAmount

correct_families.description: RANK or DENSE_RANK keeps every tied row.
reference_sql: SELECT t.CustomerID, t.AccountNumber, t.OrderID, t.OrderDate, t.TotalAmount
FROM (SELECT c.CustomerID, c.AccountNumber, o.OrderID, o.OrderDate, o.TotalAmount,
RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY o.CustomerID ORDER BY o.OrderDate DESC) AS rk
JOIN qe.Orders o ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID

traps.why: ROW_NUMBER keeps one row per customer. About 4% of Gold customers lose tied latest orders.
traps.told_apart_by: A customer with two orders on the same latest OrderDate.
example_sql: SELECT t.CustomerID, t.AccountNumber, t.OrderID, t.OrderDate, t.TotalAmount
FROM (SELECT c.CustomerID, c.AccountNumber, o.OrderID, o.OrderDate, o.TotalAmount,
ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY o.CustomerID ORDER BY o.OrderDate DESC) AS rk
JOIN qe.Orders o ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID

traps.why: TOP (1) without WITH TIES returns one of the tied orders, with or without a tiebreaker.
traps.told_apart_by: A customer with two orders on the same latest OrderDate.
example_sql: SELECT c.CustomerID, c.AccountNumber, lo.OrderID, lo.OrderDate, lo.TotalAmount

traps.why: OUTER APPLY returns Gold customers that have no orders, with NULL order columns.
traps.told_apart_by: A Gold customer with no orders.
example_sql: SELECT c.CustomerID, c.AccountNumber, lo.OrderID, lo.OrderDate, lo.TotalAmount
SELECT TOP (1) WITH TIES o.OrderID, o.OrderDate, o.TotalAmount

min_improvement.basis: Two full passes over Orders and a spilling aggregate (9 minutes) against about 150k short ordered seeks.

key.reference_notes: Adding only the index is acceptable for speed. IX_Orders_CustomerID cannot give OrderDate order or TotalAmount.
